mechanism: Every upstream is a hardcoded literal, so the probe replaces the `node-fetch` module and the global `fetch` with a controlled peer; the Go side replays the same peer through a real listener. The pinned child clock is frozen through NODE_OPTIONS so the RS256 JWT is deterministic and comparable byte for byte.

fields.reason: the pinned handler propagates the PROVIDER status on a provider error and answers 500 elsewhere
audio/wav for audio/l16, the provider mime type otherwise
JSON answers are compared as text, including the two distinct error shapes
audio answers are compared by digest and length; a UTF-8 round trip would corrupt the RIFF header bytes
four auth branches build four URL shapes, including the raw model interpolation
the token request carries the JWT assertion, compared byte for byte against the deterministic RS256 output
x-goog-api-key or Authorization: Bearer, asserted in both directions by the test
the full branch makes two requests per call (token, then model) and never caches

the pinned handler merges GEMINI_SAFETY with VERTEX_SAFETY from constants.js; the fixture records the merged array but the Go side is expected to reproduce it verbatim once those constants are ported, so only its shape is asserted here

normalizations: The pinned clock is frozen at 2023-11-14T22:13:20.000Z so `iat`/`exp` and therefore the whole JWT are deterministic.
The service-account private key is a synthetic 2048-bit key embedded in the probe; no real credential is recorded.
